newsitem.title: INDIA: India's debt service ratio hits low - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India's debt service ratio hits low - Chidambaram.

text.p: India's debt service ratio has fallen to an all time low of 21 percent of total exports, Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Thursday.

"Debt service ratio as a proportion of current receipts has also declined to an all time low of 21 percent," Chidamabaram said, addressing a Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry award ceremony, while listing improvements in India's economy.
But, he said total public debt was 64 percent of gross domestic product and external debt had fallen to 28 percent.
"We are spending money that we do not have. We are borrowing money from the next generation," the finance minister said.
He said that after factoring in non-planned expenditure he was faced with a budget already 26 billion rupees ($726 million) in deficit, before even accounting for planned expenditure.
"Stricly speaking, I have no right to make a plan. I'm already in debt by 26 billion," he said.
"Yet I make a plan (to spend) for 620 billion and how do I get out of it... I borrow 650 billion," Chidambaram said, rhetorically asking how long this situation was sustainable.

He cited a study showing subsidies accounted for 15 percent of GDP in 1994/96, but said not all subsidies should be eliminated, particularly where they were aimed at helping India's 300 million poor people.
He said the disinvesment commission had produced three reports embracing 15 public sector companies and added plans were afoot to sell of stakes in three but did not identify them.
"Soon I hope we can begin disinvesting in three of these 15 companies," he said.
Chidambaram has budgeted to raise 48 billion rupees from disinvestment in 1997/98 (April-March).
He said the public sector needed restructuring and reform to improve on a paltry 3.5 percent return on investment.
The finance minister implored private industry to invest in preparation for an expected increase in demand, and take advantage of low tax rates, low interest rates and high liquidity.
He said his budget measures to cut taxes and lower tariffs should stimulate demand and encourage people to save.

Chidambaram said in the first six weeks of the current financial year aggregate bank deposits increased by 100.8 billion rupees and in the last two weeks may have increased by another 40 billion rupees.
